produced_reading: Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at LOW intensity (soft but slightly stronger than gen). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically. The intensity modifier 'lo' follows the same scale: gen < lo < mod < firm < hi.

Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at MODERATE intensity (the default middle level). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically. 'mod' is the default intensity and would normally be omitted per our convention.
Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at GENTLE/soft intensity (the lowest intensity level: gen < lo < mod < firm < hi). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically.
Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at HIGH/maximum intensity (the strongest level on our scale). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically.

Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at FIRM intensity (strong, below hi on the scale: gen < lo < mod < firm < hi). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically. This is the intensity modifier seen most often in LP instructions (e.g. 'LP>BT firm 20s').

Lamp (LP) combined with the symptom code BR (too bright). Parsed compositionally: lamp tool applied to a too-bright condition, or lamp directed at a bright face. This is not a valid instruction form — BR is a symptom descriptor, not a face code or intensity modifier, so the combination is grammatically ill-formed in our code system.

Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at LOW intensity (soft but slightly stronger than gen). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically. The intensity modifier 'lo' follows the same scale: gen < lo < mod < firm < hi.
Lamp placed at the specified face's side, aimed inward, at HIGH/maximum intensity (the strongest level on our scale). Opposite face receives ambient/dim light automatically.

Lamp (LP) combined with the symptom code DM (too dim). Parsed compositionally: lamp tool applied to a dim condition, or lamp directed at a dim face. Like LP BR, DM is a symptom descriptor rather than a face code or intensity modifier, making this form grammatically ill-formed in our code system.
